means: A wide gap between the darkest and brightest parts of the frame - blacks that are properly black, highlights that are properly bright, and less in the middle.
does: As a tag it deepens shadows and lifts highlights and reads hard, graphic, unforgiving. It is real danbooru vocabulary and one of the better-behaved quality words here, because contrast is something the model genuinely learned to draw in cel art. It is far better as a GRADE, though, where it is exact: studio/looks/bleach.json is eq=contrast=1.35:saturation=0.45, noir.json is contrast 1.32 over a true greyscale (measured SATAVG exactly 0.000, which is why that steep a curve is safe there). The project position is blunt - grading is deterministic, prompting is not. One hazard: these filters MULTIPLY. Contrast in the look, plus hot at contrast 1.10 and saturation 1.18, plus glow, is how a third of a film went magenta, which is why every high-contrast look here takes saturation DOWN to leave headroom.
reach_for_it: for noir, threat, heat, bleach-bypass grit - and set it in the look's grade string, treating the tag as a bonus
used_in: the tag strings and grades of studio/looks/bleach.json, bleach_bypass.json and noir.json; the low_key and bleach_bypass options of studio/cards/grade_preset.json
